newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-STANKOWSKI TAKES ONE-SHOT LEAD AT KAPALUA INTERNATIONAL.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-STANKOWSKI TAKES ONE-SHOT LEAD AT KAPALUA INTERNATIONAL.

text.p: Paul Stankowski fired a six-under-par 67 Saturday to grab a one-shot lead after the third round of the $1.1 million Kapalua International.

Stankowski, who started the round in a four-way tie for second, tamed the Plantation Course to move to 16-under-par 201 through 54 holes, one shot better than U.S. Open champion Steve Jones and former tournament winner Bob Gilder.
The 56-man field used both the Plantation and Bay courses over the first two rounds, but are playing the final 36 holes at the par-73 Plantation layout.
Jones and Gilder, who shared the lead after each of the first two rounds, both shot four-under-par 69s for 202 totals.

Two-time former champion Fred Couples, one of four players forced to complete their second rounds early this morning after Friday's heavy rains interrupted play, also shot 69 to stand two shots off the pace.
Briton Sandy Lyle, Scott McCarron and Billy Mayfair were three shots behind at 204.

Stankowski, who won his first U.S. PGA tournament in April with a playoff victory at the BellSouth Classic, had six birdies during a bogey-free round Saturday, including three in a row beginning at the par-5 fifth hole.
Jones, like Gilder, had five birdies against one bogey and called it a "ho-hum day."
"Nothing great happened," he said. "The bogey kind of soured my round."
The Kapalua International, which offers a top prize of $198,000, is not a sanctioned PGA event and the top five players on the PGA money list skipped it, as did 20-year-old Tiger Woods.
The Plantation Course is a 7,263-yard layout. The par-71 Bay Course measures 6,600 yards.
